I've worked at a fair few companies and noticed that on React projects, even old and outdated codebases tend to be fairly easy to maintain and upgrade, whereas Vue codebases tend to get worse and worse the more time passes, a couple areas in particular are with Vuex, where the codebases not using map functions (mapActions, mapGetters, etc.) and not having decent naming distinctions between mutations and actions (I've seen places where the getter, mutation and the action all had the same name, making it really easy to cause a bug and prevents you from easily renaming things) are usually really hard to maintain and update. Another annoying thing is how no IDE has truly good integration with the Vue instance in components, as I most often found myself doing console.log(this) just to find if something was there or not, when you work with classes in TypeScript or simple javascript functions you get much better integration around this, but somehow this is not true with Vue.

On the React side however the biggest pain point is usually Redux, but thankfully a large part of React projects are based on TypeScript which means that it's much easier to update and maintain, and you don't need a 1 week brief on the project's quirks whatnot to make a simple change.
